learningObjective: Precisely define compile-time kernel selection and identify its inputs.

canonicalClaims.claim: Kernel selection maps each op-instance (with its concrete shape, dtype, layout, and target attributes) to a specific implementation candidate — library call, generated kernel, or fused template — using a cost model or measurement-based ranking.
conditions: The op-instance has concrete attributes at compile time (or a bounded dynamic-shape range).
A catalog of candidate implementations exists for the op-type.
nonImplications: Does not imply optimality of the selection; the cost model may be approximate.
Does not imply the selection is fixed at load time — some systems re-select at runtime for extreme shape variance.

misconceptions.claim: Kernel selection is a runtime dispatch step that happens at every kernel launch.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Selection is typically a compile-time step; runtime dispatch is a distinct concept (e.g., algorithm autoselector for a specific batch).

misconceptions.claim: Kernel selection is the choice of which shared library to link at build time.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Link-time library resolution is a build concern, unrelated to per-op kernel selection.

misconceptions.claim: Kernel selection is another name for structured pruning of the model's weights.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Pruning modifies the model; kernel selection maps op-instances to implementations without changing weights.

misconceptions.claim: For a given op type and shape, there is always one uniquely best kernel; kernel selection is deterministic.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Multiple candidates often exist with comparable performance; measurement noise and cost-model approximation lead to non-deterministic winners across runs.

implementationFacts: cuBLAS Lt provides a heuristic-based algorithm selector for GEMMs.
TorchInductor evaluates ATen, mm-out (cuBLAS), and Triton candidates at compile time.
TVM Relax dispatches to library-external or generated kernels through the `dispatch` pass.
performanceScenarios: For M=K=N=4096 FP16 GEMM on A100, kernel selection typically picks a cuBLAS Tensor Core algorithm.
For small batched GEMV, generated Triton kernels can beat library defaults.
